title: Amherst vs Wesleyan: tuition, size, location
summary: Amherst College (Amherst) versus Wesleyan University (Wesleyan). Also searched as Wesleyan vs Amherst. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Wesleyan University and Amherst College are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes reported by College Scorecard. Wesleyan University, located in Middletown, has an undergraduate enrollment of 3,067 students, while Amherst College in Amherst enrolls 1,911 undergraduates. The tuition costs for in-state students are similar, with Wesleyan charging $70,342 and Amherst $70,480. These differences highlight variations in size and location between the two institutions.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Wesleyan University and Amherst College have comparable tuition costs for both in-state and out-of-state students, with Wesleyan charging $70,342 and Amherst $70,480. Despite the similarity in tuition fees, the median debt for students who complete their degrees differs between the two schools. Wesleyan graduates have a median debt of $17,000, whereas Amherst graduates carry a median debt of $13,740. These figures reflect the financial obligations students may expect upon completing their education at each institution.

In comparing Wesleyan University vs Amherst College, the tuition rates are nearly identical, but the median debt upon graduation is lower at Amherst. This distinction may influence prospective students considering the overall cost of attendance and post-graduation financial impact. Wesleyan vs Amherst thus presents a nuanced picture of cost, balancing tuition with student debt outcomes.
